newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia 1996/97 rice harvest sets new record.
newsitem.headline: Australia 1996/97 rice harvest sets new record.

text.p: Australia's 1996/97 rice harvest has already set a new record and with grain still being received is headed toward receivals approaching 1.4 million tonnes.
The current harvest had so far produced total receivals of 1.341 million tonnes paddy, Ricegrowers Co-operative Ltd said.
This surpassed the previous record crop of 1.13 million tonnes delivered in 1994/95.
Ricegrowers now expected receivals this year of about 1.375 million tonnes, it said.
The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics' (ABARE) official forecast for rice production in the year to June 30 1997 is 1.46 million tonnes, up from 950,000 tonnes the year before.
Continuing dry weather in Australia's rice-growing state of New South Wales has accelerated the rice harvest, which could be over in coming weeks, several months earlier than last year.
Buoyant receivals from the current crop follow a recent decision by Japan to call tenders on May 28 for the supply of 7,000 tonnes of rice.

The earlier than usual tender has been welcomed by the Australian rice-growing industry, which, because of its opposite seasons to the Northern Hemisphere, has argued that Japan should open its tenders for foreign rice early in the year and spread them more regularly throughout the 12 months.

Japan's Food Agency said on April 30, after the tender announcement, that foreign rice imports wiould be based on domestic demand and local consumers' taste and that Australia should not raise its hopes too high of increasing its share of the Japanese market.
